filePath.description: Absolute file path of the executable to debug.

tools.description: Executes a native x64dbg command string (like 'erun', 'analr', 'graph'). This is for x64dbg-internal commands ONLY — do NOT pass MCP tool names here. MCP tools (WaitForEvent, GetDebugState, Disassemble, etc.) must be called directly as tools.

tools.description: Lists the available MCP tools, optionally filtered to a single category.

count.description: Number of most recent events to return (default: all, max 64).

tools.description: Returns the last N debugger events (exceptions, breakpoints, DLL loads, thread events, etc.). Keeps the last 64 events in a ring buffer. Use this to see what happened in x64dbg.

tools.description: Clears the event log ring buffer.

tools.description: Attaches the debugger to a running process by PID.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds (default 30000, max 120000).

tools.description: Blocks until a debugger event fires (breakpoint hit, paused, resumed, exception, session start/stop) or timeout. Returns all events that occurred. Use this to monitor debugger state changes in real-time over HTTP — call it after 'run' or while waiting for the user to interact with the debugger.

tools.description: Returns the current instruction pointer (EIP/RIP), the module it belongs to, and its label/comment. Takes no arguments.

tools.description: Blocks until the debuggee stops running (hits a breakpoint, exception, or exits). Returns the reason for the pause and the current address. Use after 'run' to wait for the target to break.

tools.description: Executes a single instruction, stepping INTO any call encountered (F7). Takes no arguments.

tools.description: Executes a single instruction, stepping OVER any call/subroutine entirely (F8). Takes no arguments.

tools.description: Runs until the current function returns to its caller (Ctrl+F9). Takes no arguments.

tools.description: Pauses (suspends) the running debuggee, equivalent to Debug > Pause (F12). Takes no arguments.

tools.description: Terminates the current debugging session and closes the debuggee process. Takes no arguments.

tools.description: Restarts the current debugging session from the beginning. Takes no arguments.
